attempts.entry_title: Egg-laying rate functions and choice in Drosophila (Vijayan et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: In this data the paper's central finding holds up: after leaving a better substrate, flies hold back egg laying on a worse one and release it with time, across chamber layouts, strains and agarose hardness. Kir2.1 in DDC-Gal4 neurons erodes the sucrose choice, and D1-like receptor mutants show flat rate curves. Not reproduced are an unchanged egg-laying pause, as pauses measured by the Methods come in 0.5-s steps, and the lack of preference in D. suzukii, where one time bin differs without correction for multiple tests. The Gal4 screen, Gal80 rescues, feeding tests and most receptor mutants could not be tested, as those flies are not in the dataset. Some timing details hold only in part.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Vijayan, Wang, Chandra, Chakravorty, Li, Sarbanes, Akhlaghpour and Maimon (2022) on dandiset 000212, which holds the tracking of 1013 flies in egg-laying chambers (position, island, sucrose under the fly and egg times at 2 frames per second). It rebuilds the search periods and the egg-laying rate functions of the Methods and tests the three-choice, tunnel, middle-island, strain, agarose, DDC>Kir and receptor-mutant findings. The movable-boundary, glued-fly, screen, Gal80 rescue and feeding-latency experiments are not in the dandiset, nor are four of the six agarose conditions of Fig. 6B.

outcomes.statement: In two-choice sucrose chambers, flies leave the higher sucrose substrate in 964 of 1205 (80%) searches that start on it, and leave the lower sucrose substrate in only 918 of 2744 (33%) searches that start on it.
outcomes.source: Results, A framework for understanding how previous substrate experiences guide egg-laying choices, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: flies leave higher sucrose in 964 of 1205 or 80% of searches initiated on higher sucrose), whereas flies that start a search on lower sucrose know to stay (flies leave lower sucrose in only 918 of 2744 or 33% of searches initiated on lower sucrose) ( P < 0.001, two-sided Wilcoxon rank sum test

statistics.test: two-sided Wilcoxon rank sum test on searches as 0/1 trials
statistics.n: 1205 searches started on higher sucrose and 2744 on lower sucrose

outcomes.notes: Searches by M3 without the 30-s minimum in the CS 0/200, 0/500 and 200/500 chambers. 1205 start on the higher sucrose substrate and 970 (0.805) leave it; 2773 start on the lower and 917 (0.331) leave it; rank sum on 0/1 trials p = 8.8e-167. All four values are within tolerance. By chamber the fractions leaving higher are 0.814, 0.832 and 0.780 and leaving lower 0.353, 0.358 and 0.283; 87 of 88 flies with searches of both kinds leave the higher more often. The 1205 + 2773 = 3978 searches are all the eggs of the three chambers.
deviations: Search start (M3), taken from Methods, Automated determination of egg-laying search: the scan for the first frame below 0.1 mm/s of the 18.5-s centred boxcar of speed starts 9 s before the egg, so that the minimum search is 9 s as the passage says. This reading gives 1205 searches started on higher sucrose, the paper's number; the scan from the frame before the egg (shown) gives 1202.

The rank sum test is computed with a tie correction (scipy mannwhitneyu, asymptotic, continuity corrected), as MATLAB's ranksum does; the paper used MATLAB (Data analysis software). Without the correction p-values on 0/1 trials are far too large.

outcomes.statement: The 0 and 200 mM rate functions merge at an earlier time in three-choice chambers than in two-choice chambers.
outcomes.source: Results, Flies lay eggs on the best of three options, paragraph 3; Figure 2A to 2G
outcomes.quote: the 0 and 200 mM egg-laying rate functions did appear to merge at an earlier time point in three-choice ( Fig. 2, E to G ) compared to two-choice chambers
outcomes.notes: Merge points with visit trials are 1200, 5 and 5 s in the three three-choice chambers; the CS 0/200, 0/200/200 and five-island 0/200 chambers do not merge within 7200 s. All three three-choice chambers merge earlier under readings (a) and (b). With the 10 to 15 s bin first, they merge at 1200, 10 and not at all (visit trials) or 1200, 10 and 300 s (search trials), so two or three of three are still earlier. The support is thin. The merges at 5 s rest on bins with almost no eggs (0 of 42 against 0 of 48 visits in 0/500/500/500/200; 4 of 854 against 0 of 715 in 0/500/200/500/200), and the bins after them differ up to 60 s (p = 0.011 or less from 15 to 60 s in the first, p < 0.001 from 10 to 60 s in the second). Later the first chamber's curves come together (60 to 90 s p = 0.013, 90 to 150 s p = 0.051, then 0.085 to 0.781), while the second's differ in every bin (p = 0.002 and 0.006 at 300 to 600 and 600 to 1200 s, the others below 0.001). The merge at 10 s is of the same kind (1 of 189 against 1 of 158). Only the 1200 s merge of 0/500/200 follows bins with many eggs.

outcomes.quote: In this chamber, flies laid eggs even more rapidly upon entering the 0 mM side

outcomes.statement: Across the 4-mm, 2-mm and 2-mm bounce chambers, flies spend progressively more time on 200 mM before entering 0 mM and laying a fast egg (within 10 s), with medians of 54, 96 and 576 s over 36, 44 and 23 eggs.
outcomes.source: Results, Flies lay eggs more rapidly on high-quality substrates, paragraph 2; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: Medians are 54, 96, and 576 s for increasing shades of gray. Thirty-six, 44, and 23 eggs for increasing shades of gray.
outcomes.notes: Fast eggs (on 0 mM within 10 s of entering it from 200 mM) number 36, 44 and 22 in the 4-mm, 2-mm and bounce chambers, within tolerance of 36, 44 and 23, and the median duration of the preceding 200 mM visit increases, 45.5, 57.0 and 379.5 s, but all three medians are below the tolerances around 54, 96 and 576 s. Bounce differs from both others (p = 0.003); 4 mm and 2 mm do not (p = 0.54). Other dwell measures tried while preparing (cumulative 200 mM time since a 0 mM visit of 5 s or more, 200 mM time since the previous egg) did not give the paper's medians either; they are not run here. Brief visits are common at the boundary (359 of 12154 sucrose visits in the 4-mm chamber last one frame), but merging visits of up to 0.5, 1, 2 or 5 s into the visits around them gives medians of 48.5, 57.0 and 441.5 s (448.2 s at 5 s) with 35, 44 and 21 (or 20) fast eggs, still outside every median tolerance. For the 2-mm and bounce chambers flicker does not explain the short medians; for the 4-mm chamber it nearly does, as the merged median, 48.5 s, is 0.1 s below the lower tolerance of 48.6 s.
deviations: No frame of the tunnel chambers lacks a sucrose label (printed), so the first frame on 0 mM follows the last on 200 mM and 'within 10 s' from crossing the midline and from leaving 200 mM are the same frame; both readings of the criterion are one here. Counting eggs strictly under 10 s gives 34, 42 and 18 with the same medians.

The rank sum test is computed with a tie correction (scipy mannwhitneyu, asymptotic, continuity corrected), as MATLAB's ranksum does; the paper used MATLAB (Data analysis software). Without the correction p-values on 0/1 trials are far too large.

outcomes.statement: Pooling the three tunnel chambers, the egg-laying rate in the 10 s after entering 0 mM rises when flies have not experienced 0 mM for more than about 4 min.
outcomes.source: Results, Flies lay eggs more rapidly on high-quality substrates, paragraph 2; Figure 3E
outcomes.quote: we observe that flies increase their egg-laying rate upon entering 0 mM specifically if they have not experienced 0 mM for >~4 min
outcomes.notes: Pooled tunnel chambers, first 10 s on 0 mM within a search: 1.213 eggs/min after a previous 200 mM visit of at least 240 s (25 eggs in 140 visits) against 0.345 after shorter visits (69 in 1280), p = 1.8e-08. Below 240 s the bin rates are 0.245 to 0.406 except 150 to 240 s (0.922); Spearman rho of rate against bin order 0.42, p = 0.20. The higher rate after long absences holds in each chamber (1.08, 1.18, 1.37 against 0.19, 0.65, 0.87). The no-rising-trend part holds only on that reading: the 150 to 240 s bin is already high (0.922 against 0.316 eggs/min below 150 s, p = 0.0014); over the bins from 5 s rho = 0.68, p = 0.029; with visits of up to 0.5 s merged (boundary flicker) the 0 to 5 s bin loses its 2 eggs and rho = 0.74, p = 0.009 over all bins below 240 s. Below 150 s the rates are flat under every variant (p = 0.11 to 0.21). The rise is present but starts between 150 and 240 s (2.5 to 4 min), below the 240 s edge the claims file fixes. The case is borderline, as the paper says "~4 min" and the 150 to 240 s bin holds 9 eggs.
deviations: The rank sum test is computed with a tie correction (scipy mannwhitneyu, asymptotic, continuity corrected), as MATLAB's ranksum does; the paper used MATLAB (Data analysis software). Without the correction p-values on 0/1 trials are far too large.

'No rising trend' below 240 s has no test in the paper. Assumed: it fails when the bin just below 240 s, 150 to 240 s, has a higher rate than the bins below 150 s by the rank sum test (M5) at p < 0.05. This step test decides the outcome. The Spearman correlations of bin rate with bin order are shown as variants only; the first version of this attempt used the one over all bins from 0 s, which shows no rise (p = 0.20) and would give reproduced. The notebook shows every reading.

outcomes.statement: D. suzukii shows no measurable egg-laying preference for lower sucrose; its rates on 0 and 200 mM are similar in a two-choice chamber.

outcomes.notes: A claim of absence on the bin test at p < 0.05. One of 13 bins from 5 s on, 300 to 600 s, has a higher rate on 0 than on 200 mM at p = 0.029 (13 of 17 visits against 8 of 20; 0.94 against 0.55 eggs/min), under both trial readings. Whether the criterion should correct for the number of bins is asked of a reader (questions/vijayan-2022.yaml).

A log-link Poisson fit of the same kernel is shown as a variant and gives the same result.

findings.statement: The four agarose groups carry an Agarose_Percentage series, the agarose under the fly in every frame, which the other groups lack; its label changes only with the island. The 0.8 against 1.4% chambers were loaded both ways round (island 0 is 0.8% for 18 of 24 flies without sucrose and 12 of 24 with 200 mM on both sides), so the island number alone does not give the hardness, but the series does. The first version of this attempt read only the island and sucrose series, missed it, and reported the hardness as unrecorded (metadata_insufficient, major); that was wrong, and this finding replaces it.

The paper says all fly tracking data it used are on DANDI 000212, but the dandiset lacks the movable-boundary chambers (Fig. 1D, E), the glued flies (Fig. 1F), the 115-line Gal4 screen (Fig. 7A), the Gal80 rescues (Fig. 7L to N), nine of the 13 receptor genotypes of Fig. 8A, the 200/500 mM and agarose chambers of the mutants and DDC>Kir flies (Fig. 8J, K), four of the six agarose conditions of Fig. 6B and the BDSC 84714 mutant. Some of these may have been scored by egg counts without tracking; the paper does not say. The feeding-latency videos (Figs. 7B, 8B) are not tracking data and are also absent.

The two Dop1R2 groups are named 'Dop1R2-mutant-1' and '-2', with genotypes that name only the paper each mutant came from (Keleman et al. 2012, Deng et al. 2019). The paper's allele names (Dop1R2 attP, Dop1R2-) follow from its references and the egg counts, not from the files.
Every file has the same placeholder session start time (2021-01-01 01:01:01 -05:00), so the files hold no recording dates and experiments cannot be ordered or matched to batches.

48 of 29531 intervals between successive eggs of a fly are under 10 s (12 are a single frame), against the paper's statement that eggs are at least 1 min apart; in 47 both eggs are on one island and in 34 the fly moves no faster than 0.3 mm/s between them, so they may be double annotations. They are listed in the data check and kept.
The dandiset has never been published: only the draft exists, so it has no fixed version or DOI, and an attempt on it can only record the draft's modification time (2023-06-20T00:56:15Z).

Egg counts per group agree with the egg-aligned counts of the paper's legends within 2 eggs in 16 of 19 groups (for example 1863 against 1862 for CS 0/200, 533 for DDC>Kir 31 C, 831 and 795 for the same-agarose chambers). The files hold 596 eggs against 586 for Dop1R2-mutant-1, 220 against 214 for D. suzukii and 670 against 675 for the bounce chamber; the legends' counts are of egg-aligned averages that leave out eggs near the ends of a recording, and those built here hold 586, 216 and 670. The ref. 16 chambers hold 95 flies and 3978 eggs (paper 95, 3979), no recording appears twice, the islands follow the y position and the sucrose label changes only with the island, and flies speed up before an annotated egg and pause at it while shifted times show no such contrast, so the egg annotations share the position clock.

Two Dop1R2-mutant-1 recordings (sub-0-200-Dop1R2-mutant-1-fly#-11 and -12) have 6 and 4 eggs annotated in their last 19 s, 0.5 to 10.5 s apart, while the fly walks at up to 8.7 and 7.0 mm/s; they are unlikely to be eggs. They make up 7 of the 48 intervals under 10 s, and the group holds 596 eggs in all. The paper's legend count for the group, 586, is of an egg-aligned average that leaves out eggs near the ends of a video, so it does not show whether the paper counted them. They are kept; they change no outcome (fig8fg egg-count p-values 0.34 to 0.69 without them).

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors: the merge point is 'the first bin past 5 s for which P > 0.05' (Fig. 5A legend). Does the 5 to 10 s bin count as past 5 s? This attempt assumed it does; with the 10 to 15 s bin first, the DDC>Kir 31 C curves merge at the first bin and fig7cf would be reproduced in full.

Question for the authors: what is a trial in the bin test (Methods, Statistics), one visit to a time bin or one search that enters it? Most results agree; the TUT merge point is 20 s with visits and 90 s with searches.

Question for the authors: how was the dwell time of Fig. 3D measured? The duration of the 200 mM visit before a fast egg gives medians of 45.5, 57 and 379.5 s against the legend's 54, 96 and 576 s, with the same egg counts.

Question for the authors: the pause time of Methods, Statistics (from the 1-s smoothed speed rising above 0.1 mm/s before the egg) has medians of 0.5 to 2.5 s on these files. Was the speed computed or smoothed differently, or the threshold applied to another signal? The comparisons of pause medians (fig3f, fig7ik) depend on it.

Question for the authors: the search start scans back from 9 s before the egg in this attempt, which gives the paper's 1205 searches on higher sucrose; was that the procedure? And how were the fig. S4 kernel (ref. 82) and the constants k1, k2 of model 2 fit? The analysis code is not public.

entries.title: Egg-laying rate functions and choice in Drosophila (Vijayan et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Vijayan, Wang, Chandra, Chakravorty, Li, Sarbanes, Akhlaghpour and Maimon (2022) on dandiset 000212, which holds the tracking of 1013 flies in egg-laying chambers (position, island, sucrose under the fly and egg times at 2 frames per second). It rebuilds the search periods and the egg-laying rate functions of the Methods and tests the three-choice, tunnel, middle-island, strain, agarose, DDC>Kir and receptor-mutant findings. The movable-boundary, glued-fly, screen, Gal80 rescue and feeding-latency experiments are not in the dandiset, nor are four of the six agarose conditions of Fig. 6B.
